content.what_it_is: MATLAB 스크립트로 netCDF 파일을 읽기 전용으로 열고 전체 변수·속성을 순회해 헤더 정보를 표시하며(L23-L62), 각 변수를 그 netCDF 이름의 workspace 변수로 동적 생성한다. scale_factor가 발견된 변수에는 scale과 offset을 적용하려고 한다(L36-L59). 이후 생성되었다고 가정한 Band1, lat, lon에서 수심 배열을 그리고 고정 인덱스 영역을 잘라 세 ASCII 파일로 저장한 뒤 확대 영역을 다시 그린다(L64-L91).

io.name: netCDF global counts and unlimited dimension

unresolved: Only flag is reset per variable at L39. offset is assigned only when add_offset is encountered at L44-L46, while flag is enabled solely by scale_factor at L47-L50; the scaled expression at L55 can therefore use an unassigned offset for the first scale-only variable or a stale offset from an earlier variable, and an add_offset-only variable takes the unscaled branch at L57 and ignores its offset.
netcdf.open creates ncid at L25, but no netcdf.close or cleanup appears through EOF L94, so the file handle remains open after the script finishes or errors.

The fixed crop dep(2000:8000,1:6500) at L72-L77 and matching lat/lon slices at L78-L79 have no bounds checks against the dimensions loaded at L29/L37; smaller or differently ordered datasets produce out-of-range failures or wrong spatial subsets.

Variable data are assigned with eval from raw netCDF varname at L55/L57; names that are not valid MATLAB identifiers, collide with script state such as i/scale/offset, or contain executable syntax can fail or overwrite control variables before later iterations.

Post-processing assumes dynamically created variables named exactly Band1, lat, and lon at L64, L66, L78, and L79, but the enumeration loop accepts arbitrary netCDF schemas and never verifies that these three variables exist or have dimensions consistent with the transpose at L64.
strmatch at L44 and L47 performs prefix-style matching rather than an explicit exact attribute-name comparison, so similarly prefixed attributes can be mistaken for add_offset or scale_factor.
